html:
Agustín Farabundo Martí was a Salvadoran communist leader who was shot by the army on 1 February 1932, after the failed peasant rising that led to La Matanza.

The son of a landowner, he studied law and was exiled for his politics. He fought for a time with Augusto César Sandino against the American occupation of Nicaragua, then returned to organise workers and peasants as a leader of the Communist Party of El Salvador. He was arrested days before the rising of January 1932, which went ahead without him, and was executed by firing squad.

In 1980 the five guerrilla groups of the Salvadoran Civil War united as the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front, the FMLN. It became a political party after the peace of 1992 and held the presidency from 2009 to 2019.
